newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Moslem party rejects Serb vote results in advance.
newsitem.headline: Moslem party rejects Serb vote results in advance.

text.p: Bosnia's main Moslem party said on Saturday it would not recognise election results from Serb-controlled territory although they had yet to be announced.

President Alija Izetbegovic's Party of Democratic Action (SDA) charged in a letter to the U.N. Security Council that there had been serious irregularities and a lack of conditions for free and fair voting in the Bosnian Serb entity.

"The international community, in particular the sponsors of the Dayton agreement, had promised that the necessary conditions would exist at least by the date of the elections," said the letter, signed by senior SDA official Halid Genjac.

"Even before the results of the vote are known, it is clear that in many parts of Bosnia, specifically the Serb entity, the necessary conditions did not exist to provide for free and fair elections under the criteria established by Dayton or even the marginal standards of democracy."

"These irregularities and the lack of the necessary conditions for free and fair elections have decisively flawed the vote. For the above reasons the SDA deems the results of the elections in the Serb entity to be legally invalid."

The letter was released to reporters as international organisers extended polling in some areas by three hours after the official 7 p.m. (1700 GMT) close, citing technical problems which had delayed voting.
